tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

# vc-x1-messages v0.3.3

Messages for the vc-x1 family. The open threads are the inbox, the history is the archive.

One shared repo every participant can reach is the only thing the protocol assumes. A thread is
one file, appended by everyone who takes part in it, so reading a conversation is reading one
file, and a search for a message's id returns everything ever said under it. Every member's
`custom.md` points at this file, and taking part means following it, pushes included.

## Terminology

Each term stands alone, a term that relies on another follows it, and a kind of a term sits
under it.

- **Member**: a participant, named by its project's name, `vc-x1`, `iiac-perf`, `zc-ring-x1`.
- **Thread**: one conversation, the file `open/m-<tid>.md` while open and `closed/m-<tid>.md`
  after, headed `# m-<tid> <title>`, each of its lines an `m-<tid>-<num>`, so `rg -w m-<tid>`
  returns the whole thread. The directory is the thread's state, and any member may write a line
  in any open thread.
- **Thread id**: `<tid>`, an integer, never reused.
  - Its store is the tracked file `threads`, one integer, the last id issued, never decreased.
  - The opener reads it, adds one, writes it back, and takes the new value, in the opening commit.
- **Title**: the opener's, a few words, never changed.
- **Line**: one message or mark, one physical line, always, appended oldest first directly
  under the heading, no blank line anywhere in the file:
  `- m-<tid>-<num> <time> from <author> <action> <info>`.
- **Number**: `<num>`, an integer from 0, one more than the last line in the file, so the thread
  is its own counter and nothing else stores it: line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, and
  the next number is the file's line count less one. Every `m-<tid>-<num>` is unique and the numbers
  order the thread, so a search for one returns the line and every later line that names it. An
  id, thread or line, is final once written, since one clone mints them (see What is not here),
  and a rejected push, which only a second clone causes, renumbers before pushing again.
- **Time**: when the line was written, UTC to the second, `2026-09-09T16:05:42Z`. For a human
  reading the thread, never for ordering, as clocks may not agree.
- **Author**: the member who wrote the line, after the word `from`, which is there for the human
  eye, since the position already says it.
- **Action**: what the line does, one of two:
  - **`to`**: a message. Info is the recipients, comma-joined with no spaces, a space, then the
    text. A recipient need not have been in the thread before, so a forward is a `to` naming the
    new member and saying what is forwarded. A reply begins its text with the id it answers when
    position alone would leave that ambiguous, as in a thread of three.
  - **`done`**: a mark, no info. The author has nothing to say to the lines before it. Any line
    from a member clears what was pending for them, so this is the line for when there is
    nothing else to write, and the closer's last word.
- **Info**: the message text, or its title and a message-link to its body,
  `[<title>](m-<tid>-<num>.md)`, relative to the thread's own directory so the link survives
  the close.
- **Body**: `m-<tid>-<num>.md` beside its thread, for a message that wants more than a line. It
  begins `# m-<tid>-<num> <title>`, so a search for the id finds it and the heading is an anchor,
  and it ends at the end of the file. Full markdown inside, headings, lists, and code blocks, and
  a quoted line is inert since a body is never read for lines. Moved with its thread.
- **Addressed**: a member is addressed by every `to` line naming them in its recipient field,
  and by nothing else. A member named in a line's text or in a body is referenced, never
  addressed, so a tool computing pending reads the recipient field, not the whole line.
- **Pending**: for a member, every `to` line naming them numbered above their latest line in
  that thread, of either action, all of them when they have written none. Their open
  obligations, and what Read messages returns: a line stays pending until they write after it,
  however many times it has been read, and a later line naming them makes them pending again.
  So a reply is its author's own clearance, and a question back puts the ball in the other
  court until the answer comes.
- **Complete**: every addressed member has a line numbered above every `to` line naming them.
  Computed from the file alone.
- **Closed**: the file is under `closed/`, moved there whole with its bodies, so every thread
  ever is in the tree, in this file's shape, and a reader parses one shape. History is
  provenance, never a store. A closed thread takes no line, and a late thought opens a new
  thread naming the old id.
- **Message-link**: a live link within this repo, `[<text>](<file>#<slug>)`, relative to the
  linking file and resolving to whatever the reader's checkout holds. The form for a body.
- **Sha-link**: a URL naming a commit SHA (`blob/<sha>/<path>#<slug>`), never a branch, which
  moves or dies. The form for content in another repo, where only a commit is durable.
- **Clone**: one, on one machine, one owner at a time, since the ids are allocated under its
  mutex (see What is not here). `owner` (gitignored) holds `<time> take|release <member>` lines,
  the time in a line's form, UTC to the second, and the last line names the owner. It is not a
  dotfile, so an `ls` shows who holds the clone.
- **Take ownership**: append a `take` line to `owner`. Yours until released. A `take` with no
  `release` after it means a session is writing, or died writing, and only a human tells the two
  apart and clears the second by writing the release.
- **Release ownership**: rewrite `owner` to the one `release` line, so the file holds at most
  the last release and the current take, and never grows. The clone is free.

## Read Actions

### Read messages

This is a read only action, no ownership and no fetch.

1. For each thread file, `open/m-<tid>.md` and never a body `open/m-<tid>-<num>.md`, find the
   `to` lines naming you. One numbered above your latest line in that file is pending, and the
   thread is the context to read it in.
2. Nothing pending, and `owner` shows no owner: consider doing a Fetch.

A tool may do the search. The rule is the file, and the tool is a convenience.

### Find a thread

Every thread is in the tree, under `open/` or `closed/`.

- Titles: `head -1 open/*.md closed/*.md`. Titles and openers: `head -2`.
- One thread: `cat open/m-<tid>.md` or `cat closed/m-<tid>.md`, `rg -w m-<tid>` for both and
  its bodies.
- A thread's commits, each titled with the thread ids it touched:
  `git log --oneline -- open/m-<tid>.md closed/m-<tid>.md`.

## Write Actions

Every write runs inside these guards, in order:

- `Read messages` first, so the write answers the traffic as it stands.
- Read `owner`: no other member has taken ownership.
- Any guard failing: show the user and ask how to proceed.
- Re-read `owner` before releasing, and a `take` after yours means stop and show both lines.
- A rejected push: work with the user to correct the situation.

Every write is an append: a thread file grows at its end, a body is a new file, and `threads` is
the one value that is overwritten. Nothing edits a line or a body once written.

1. Take ownership.
2. Do any number of the actions below, in any threads: open, write lines, close. Each line
   follows its own rule, and the mutex serializes the write, not the action.
3. Release ownership. A commit is optional for lines: the mutex serializes the writers and a
   line carries its author and time, so an uncommitted line is as visible and as final as a
   pushed one, and the working copy may hold lines from several takes. Who commits is the
   humans' call, the member closing a thread the default, and the commit takes the working copy
   whole, titled with the ids of the threads it touches, ascending, `m-3 m-4`, whatever it does
   in them, lines, bodies, or a close, since the diff says which and the title is a convenience,
   never a store. Push when connected, since the remote is the copy no session can lose and the
   target every sha-link needs. A version commit is never optional (see Versions).

### Fetch

1. Ask the user, unless their permission is standing.
2. `git fetch`, or `jj git fetch --ignore-working-copy`, since a bare jj command snapshots the
   working copy, and that is a write.

### Open a thread

1. Read `threads`, add one, write it back. That is the thread id.
2. Create `open/m-<tid>.md`: the heading and the opener's `to` line, numbered 0, with its body
   file when it has one.

### Write a line

Follows Read messages. A reply, a forward, or a `done`, each a line, and each clears its
author's pending on its own. A reply answers everything the lines it clears asked, naming each
by id, accepted or not, and what it does not accept is said to the asker, so they are pending
again and the exchange runs until both agree or the humans settle it. What a message asks for
is done in the author's own project's records, a Todo or a cycle, which outlive the thread, and
the reply links the outcome by sha-link.

1. The thread file exists under `open/`. One under `closed/` takes no line.
2. Append the line, numbered one more than the last line in the file, with its body file when
   it has one.

### Close a thread

The opener's to do, or any addressed member's when the opener has gone quiet, once the thread
is complete. The closer's `done`, when the last line names the closer, is what completes it,
and the close sits in the same commit.

1. Move `open/m-<tid>.md` and its bodies, `open/m-<tid>-*.md`, to `closed/`.

## What is not here

- No inbox file. What is pending for a member is a query over `open/`, so a lost or stale inbox
  cannot disagree with the threads.
- No counter file per thread. The next number is read from the thread itself.
- No format version in the lines. The README's version is the rules', fields are additive,
  and a reader takes what is there.
- No second machine. The thread ids and line numbers are allocated under one clone's mutex, so
  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times
  are UTC to the second. The migration restored `m-1` from history without its blank line, its
  surplus `done` marks still valid lines.
- v0.3.0, the cutover from v0.2.0's records and inboxes: every record was complete, so no
  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

## Specimen

`open/m-41.md`, opened by abc to def and ghi, answered by both, and complete: ghi's line at 1
and def's at 2 are above 0, the line naming them, and abc's `done` at 3 is above 1 and 2, the
lines naming abc. `threads` holds 41 or more. Line 2 has a body, `open/m-41-2.md` beside it,
shown after it.

```
# m-41 hello
- m-41-0 2026-09-09T16:00:00Z from abc to def,ghi hello
- m-41-1 2026-09-09T16:05:42Z from ghi to abc hi
- m-41-2 2026-09-09T16:09:12Z from def to abc [hey, and the cycle that answers it](m-41-2.md)
- m-41-3 2026-09-09T16:12:30Z from abc done
```

````
# m-41-2 hey, and the cycle that answers it

The cycle landed at
https://github.com/winksaville/def/blob/0123456789ab/TODO.md#feat-the-cycle.

## What changed

- one thing
- another, with the command that shows it:

  ```
  vc-x1 validate --fast
  ```
````

# Todo and cycle record

This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record, read first at
acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.

- Check the Land: `main` at the cycle's trapezoid in both repos and on origin, the bookmark
  `feat-issue-ioring_op_nop-via-io_uring-primitives` gone locally and on origin, and `io-uring-x1
  -V` reporting `0.2.0`, the installed build's commit the landmark's.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition and
promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path

Waits on: zc-ring-x1 tagging a version, asked of it in `m-12` in `../vc-x1-messages`, checked by
`git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git` listing one. Rank once met:
the first in `## Todo`.

`zc-ring-x1` is a path dependency on `../zc-ring-x1`, so a build takes whatever that working copy
holds and a clone without the sibling does not build. Switch to `git =
"https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` at the tag, `v0.19.5` at `e705b50d` being the
commit the spsc rung was built on. `core::error::Error` for zc-ring-x1's error types, so `?` reaches
`Box<dyn Error>`, was not asked, and is a later message if it is wanted.

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).

### feat: build and install by cargo xtask

`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` in `.vc-config.md` are the project's knowledge in vc-x1's
config, as `[validate]` was before `cargo xtask validate`. Move them into xtask, `cargo xtask install
--profile dev` for one, with a `custom.md` override where the agent-files name `vc-x1 install`.

### feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags

`io-uring-x1` has a CLI, `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`, and no completion. Give it clap's
`CompleteEnv`, as xtask has, so `source <(COMPLETE=bash io-uring-x1)` registers it, and
`io-uring-x1-dev` its own the same way. The depths complete to the powers of two up to the kernel's
limits, 32768 for the SQ and 65536 for the CQ, the values the kernel rounds to. It needs
`clap_complete` with `unstable-dynamic`, as xtask's does.

content.content:
vc-x1 0.85.24+a5026b80c1b2

Run a cycle by its stages, each a flag, one command for the acts
the flow has.

--open opens a cycle: it makes the bookmark on the work @ first,
the slug of --title or --bookmark's name, kept local, then
writes the cycle's record. In TODO.md what `## Closed` holds is
deleted and the `## Todo` entry titled as --title is moved into an
`## In Progress` scaffold, an empty one when no entry matches, and
in zTOC.md the ladder is replaced with the opening and the closing.
Every check is made before anything changes: a cycle in progress is
refused, as is a name in use, and a workspace with no TODO.md or
zTOC.md, a cycle running on its record. --no-record makes the
bookmark alone, a branch the later stages will not take, as does
--bookmark without --title.
--dry-run says each edit and makes none. Nothing is committed or
pushed, and the version is the project's to bump.

--ladder makes the ladder in zTOC.md from the rung headings, the
`##### ` headings under `#### Rungs` of the cycle in progress in
TODO.md, in their order, so a rung is written once. Each line is
numbered by its position and its marker computed: `(done)` when a
commit of the rung's title is on the cycle's branch, `(current)` the
first without one. Refused, with nothing edited: a commit on the
branch that is no rung's, a rung written twice, a ladder not opened
and closed by the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing", and
a line of the ladder there that is no rung by its grammar. The
branch is the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches that no other
local bookmark does, the bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's.

--commit commits the working copies as a rung of the cycle in
progress, by the code `vc-x1 commit` runs, so a dual workspace gets
the pair, each half stamped with the other's change id. A cycle's
first commit is its opening: the title is the cycle title plus
" opening" and the body `[opening] body`, a --body given taking
its place. Any other is a work rung, which gives --title, a rung
heading not yet committed, and --body, the text or @PATH. The ladder
is rewritten first, the rung done, so the commit carries it, and the
cycle's bookmark is the one advanced, no other. -s is required: `b`
the pair, `w` the work half alone, `p` a plain repo's commit, each
checked against the workspace. --push publishes the rung on the cycle's
bookmark, a
draft. The closing is not a rung's commit, and is refused.

--close [REV,...] closes the cycle from the work @, which is on the
cycle's tip, and names its shape, --single-step or --multi-step,
which the branch's commit count checks. --single-step is the cycle's
one commit: made now from @ when the branch has none, or the opening
with the closing squashed into it when it has one, its title the bare
cycle title and its trailer kept, and refused over two or more. Its
--body is required, the commit holding the work, unless
--default-body asks for the pointer. --multi-step is a ladder, whose
closing is its own commit, the cycle title plus " closing" and
`[closing] body` unless --title or --body is given, and refused with
no opening committed.
It is linear, on @'s own parents, unless --trapezoid <BOOKMARK> makes
the destination its first parent or a REV listed joins another
head, each a parent after @'s. --dead-end, with --multi-step, titles
the closing " dead-end closing". The ladder is rewritten, every
rung done, and the record moved to `## Closed`, both in the commit.
The acceptance check comes first, by hand, and again after.

--land <BOOKMARK> lands a closed cycle on the destination, any
bookmark, none assumed: the agent @
committed when the cycle's commits name it, the destination
fast-forwarded to the cycle's last commit, and the cycle's bookmark
deleted, --skip keeping a side. The cycle is the one `## Closed`
holds, its bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's, and a cycle
still in progress is refused. A destination that moved is refused,
naming the ways on, and --merge is one: a merge commit of the
destination and the cycle's last commit, made from an empty @ and
then landed, a conflicted one undone and left to you. The stages
chain in their order, `cycle --close --multi-step --land <BOOKMARK> -s b
--push`, the
Land's checks made before the closing is. --push with --land
publishes the destination and deletes the cycle's bookmark on
origin, and without --land it is the draft push.

--push alone is a stage: it publishes what the cycle's state calls

-### feat: issue IORING_OP_NOP via io_uring primitives
-#### Problem
-The long term goal is to use io_uring as the interface to the kernel for our message
-based actor system with our latest versions of pool, mpsc and spsc in ../zc-ring-x1
-The short term goal is to start with IORING_OP_NOP ignoring our pool ... and then
-try to connect two of our spsc to and to send IORING_OP_NOP via the sqe (Submission Queue Entry)
-and receive it via cqe (Completion Queue Entry)
-Use rustix:
-- repo: https://github.com/bytecodealliance/rustix
-- docs: https://docs.rs/rustix/latest/rustix/
-More information is at Linux io_uring docs:
-- io_uring: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/io_uring.7.html
-- io_uring_enter and the opcodes: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/io_uring_enter.2.html
-#### Solution
-An io_uring built from its primitives with rustix, `Ring` in `src/ring.rs`: `io_uring_setup` at
-depths the caller chooses, the rings and the SQE array mapped, the kernel's offsets resolved into
-pointers, `push` publishing an SQE by the SQ tail, `submit` entering the ring, and `pop` copying a
-CQE out, each index ordered against the kernel's. In front of it, `Driver` in `src/driver.rs`
-carries NOPs over two zc-ring-x1 spsc queues, requests into SQEs and CQEs into completions, with
-backpressure through both, and the binary runs a caller and the driver on two threads, its depths
-set by `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`. The protocol and the memory rules it rests on are in
-[io-uring.md](notes/io-uring.md).
-The project's tasks grew alongside: validation moved from vc-x1's config into `cargo xtask
-validate`, read-only, `cargo xtask run` runs the one binary with its arguments and help passed as
-`cargo run` passes them, completion included, and the tasks became `xtask-lib`, a package of their
-own that `xtask` depends on, ready to move into a repo of its own.
-#### Acceptance check
-`cargo test` passes, including a test that pushes NOP requests, each with its own `user_data`, into
-the request spsc and reads back from the completion spsc one CQE per request, each with the matching
-`user_data` and `res` 0. Running `io-uring-x1` prints the same round trip.
-#### Deliberation
-- Primitives, not a wrapper crate: rustix's `io_uring` module supplies the syscalls and the kernel's
-  structs, and the ring setup and index handling are ours.
-  - The `io-uring` crate and liburing do the mapping and the head and tail protocol for us, and
-    learning that protocol is the point, since the actor system will drive it directly.
-- Three work rungs planned, each with its own test: the ring set up, a NOP round trip, the spsc
-  queues in front of it, and ten run.
-  - The spsc rung needs a working ring under it to test against, so the ring comes first.
-  - Seven were inserted as the work showed them, each its own commit: validation into xtask, the
-    completion script's layout, `cargo xtask run`, xtask as a library, `run`'s arguments and its
-    help as `cargo run`'s, and the queue depths. Each was small and reviewed alone, and none
-    changed the ring rungs' plan.
-- The ring holds raw pointers, one per field, not a `#[repr(C)]` mirror of the kernel's ring
-  header: the header's layout is not uapi, `io_uring_setup` gives offsets instead, and io_uring(7)'s
-  own example does the same. The entries, `io_uring_sqe` and `io_uring_cqe`, are uapi structs and
-  used as rustix gives them.
-- One mapping for both rings: we require `IORING_FEAT_SINGLE_MMAP`, which every kernel since 5.4
-  reports, and refuse a kernel without it rather than carry the two-mapping path.
-- The spsc is zc-ring-x1's by path dependency, `../zc-ring-x1`, its default version, v3.
-  - Revisited in that rung and kept for now: pinning it by git is the Todo `build: pin zc-ring-x1
-    by git, not the sibling path`, and zc-ring-x1's side, tags and `core::error::Error`, is asked
-    of it by message after this cycle lands.
-- Zero-copy across processes holds with io_uring: the kernel reads and writes a buffer at the
-  submitter's address whether its page is private or a `MAP_SHARED` region, so zc-ring-x1's pool
-  in `/dev/shm` serves as I/O buffers as it is, by the rules in [io-uring.md](notes/io-uring.md).
-- A rung inserted after the ring's: validation moves into `cargo xtask validate`, read-only.
-  - It was asked for mid-cycle, vc-x1 keeping out of the repo's content, and the old fast run
-    skipped the new library's tests, so it lands before more ring code needs validating.
-- Version 0.2.0: a feature over 0.1.0, so the opening is `0.2.0-0` and the rungs count up from it.
-#### Rungs
-The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

-##### feat: set up an io_uring with rustix
-A ring that can be set up and torn down: rustix as a dependency, `io_uring_setup`, the rings and the
-SQE array mapped, and the kernel's offsets resolved into the head, tail, mask, and array pointers,
-unmapped on drop.
-* The ring lives in a library, `src/ring.rs` under `src/lib.rs`, with `main` a client of it.
-  - The later rungs and their tests reach the ring as `io_uring_x1::ring`, and a public item is
-    never dead code while its users are still to come.
-* `Ring::new` sets up, checks `IORING_FEAT_SINGLE_MMAP`, and maps twice.
-  - The rings' mapping is sized for the larger of the SQ, ending at its index array, and the CQ,
-    ending at its CQE array, and the SQE array is its own mapping at `IORING_OFF_SQES`.
-  - The heads and tails are held as `*const AtomicU32` into the mapping, since the kernel writes
-    them concurrently, and the masks and entry counts are read once, since they never change.
-  - The SQ index array is filled once with slot i naming SQE i, so the next rung publishes an SQE
-    by its slot and never writes the array again.
-* `Ring::state` reads the indexes and sizes, the test's view and `main`'s output.
-  - The tests check the kernel's sizes, 8 SQEs and 16 CQEs, and that 5 entries round up to 8.
-* `Drop` unmaps both mappings before the fd closes, a failed `munmap` ignored as a leak at worst.
-##### feat: validate by cargo xtask
-Validation is the project's knowledge, held natively by its own tool, not by vc-x1's config:
-`cargo xtask validate` replaces `[validate]` in `.vc-config.md`, read-only, with `cargo fmt` moved

-  - vc-x1 reads `[validate]` only for `vc-x1 validate`, no cycle stage gating on it, so removing
-    the table removes that command's use here and nothing else.
-* `cargo xtask validate` runs `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy over the workspace's targets with
-  warnings denied, and `cargo test --workspace`, each announced and the first failure stopping it.
-  - Read-only: validation runs before a review, before a push, and on the closed tree, and one that
-    rewrites can change a tree after its review. `cargo fmt` is the Work step's last act instead.
-  - `--fast` is `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins`, the ring's tests now included.

-##### fix: restore clap's completion script layout
-The completion script's `COMPREPLY` line lost clap's `\` continuations, leaving runs of spaces, and
-its `IFS` holds a raw vertical tab where clap writes `$'\013'`, both an escape-processing accident
-in the copy from vc-x1. Restore clap's text in the raw string, and test for the escape as written.
-* The damage is what a non-raw string makes of clap's text: `\` and its newline dropped with the
-  next line's indent kept, and `\013` turned into the byte it names.
-  - It ran the same, bash ignoring the spaces and reading the byte inside `$''` as itself, and the
-    risk was the invisible byte, which an editor or formatter could strip and silently change the
-    word splitting of every completion.
-* The script is clap's again: `local IFS=$'\013'` as text, and the completer's environment one
-  assignment per line, joined by `\`, in the raw string where a backslash stays itself.
-* A test pins it: the escape as its four characters, no raw vertical tab, the continuations in
-  place, and no run of spaces mid-line. The printed script passes `bash -n` and completes `cx v`
-  to `version` and `validate`.
-* vc-x1's own xtask carries the same copy, `xtask/src/main.rs`, told to it only if Wink says so.
-##### feat: submit IORING_OP_NOP and reap its CQE
-A NOP round trip: an SQE written and published by the SQ tail, `io_uring_enter` to submit and wait,
-the CQE read and the CQ head advanced, each NOP's `user_data` coming back with `res` 0.
-* Each ring has one producer and one consumer, each owning one index: we own the SQ tail and the CQ
-  head, the kernel the SQ head and the CQ tail.
-  - Our own index is read `Relaxed`, since our last store is current, and the kernel's `Acquire`,
-    so the entry it covers is seen. Ours is stored `Release` after the entry is written or read,
-    so the kernel sees a whole SQE, and never reuses a CQE slot before we have copied it out.
-  - The indexes run free and wrap, a slot being the index masked, so a full SQ is `tail - head`
-    equal to the entry count, and the test runs three full rounds of a 4-entry ring to cross it.
-* `push` publishes an SQE, refusing with `SqFull` when no slot is free, `submit(want)` hands the
-  published SQEs to `io_uring_enter` and waits for `want` completions, and `pop` copies the oldest
-  CQE out as a `Completion` before advancing the head.

-    than it is offered, and `submit` returns what it took.
-  - `nop(user_data)` builds the SQE, every field zeroed but the opcode and the `user_data`.

-  safe function dereferencing any pointer it is handed would be unsound.
-* `main` sends four NOPs through an 8-entry ring and prints each completion and the indexes, all four
-  meeting at 4.

-and runs the one there is, refusing with the list when there is not exactly one.
-* The binaries are read from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, whose packages are the workspace's members,
-  each one's targets of kind `bin`, the package named as xtask's own (`CARGO_PKG_NAME`) left out,
-  so the libraries and the task runner never count.
-  - `serde_json` reads the JSON, xtask's one new dependency.
-  - Exactly one binary runs by `cargo run --bin <it> -- ARGS`, with cargo's own build output, so it
-    reads as `cargo run` does. None or several are refused, the list given, and `--bin NAME` picks
-    one, cargo then answering a wrong name with its own list.
-* ARGS come after `--` (clap's `last`), so a flag of the binary's is never taken for xtask's.
-* `run` returns nothing to print, and `main` now prints a task's text only when there is some, so
-  the binary's output is the run's last line.
-* A test feeds `binaries` a metadata sample: the one binary found with the lib and xtask left out,
-  two listed when nothing is skipped, none from empty JSON.

-package of their own, `xtask-lib`, as modules, xtask's `main` keeping the arguments and the
-dispatch, the workspace root found at runtime rather than compiled in, and what is this project's
-own passed in, not built in.
-* `xtask-lib` is its own workspace member, and `xtask` depends on it by path, so the boundary is
-  real: the binary reaches only what the library makes public.
-  - The library holds `toml_edit` and `serde_json`, and the binary only clap and the library.
-  - It has its own version, `0.1.0`, and `cargo xtask bump` sets the root package's alone, the
-    version-of-record.
-  - Named `xtask-lib`, not `xtask-x1`: `-x1` marks an experiment, dropped at 1.0, so the lasting
-    name is taken now, `-lib` telling it from each repo's `xtask` binary package.
-  - Moving it into its own repo, a path dependency becoming a git one, is the Todo `feat: share the
-    xtask library across repos`.
-* `xtask-lib/src/lib.rs` has a module per task, each with its tests beside it: `version` (the
-  version and its bump), `validate`, `run`, and `completions`, plus `cargo()` and `workspace_root()`.
-  - `xtask/src/main.rs` keeps clap's `Cli` and `Task`, the bump word candidates, the dispatch, and
-    the tests of argument parsing and completion, which need the `Cli`.
-  - Another project's xtask depends on the library and writes its own `main`, choosing its tasks.
-* The root is found at runtime by `cargo locate-project --workspace`, not compiled in from
-  `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which in a dependency would name the library's directory, not the workspace
-  using it. `cargo xtask version` from `src/` and `run` from `xtask/` both find this workspace.
-* What is a project's own is passed in: `validate` takes its commands and a label, `commands(fast)`
-  the default set, and `run` takes the package to leave out, `main` passing its own
-  `CARGO_PKG_NAME`.
-* The tests that read the real workspace stay generic, so they hold wherever the library goes: the
-  root holds a `[workspace]` manifest, and leaving out a package with binaries drops exactly its
-  binaries, whichever package that is.
-* `completions` needs no root, so a tab press runs no `cargo locate-project`.

-`cargo xtask run` takes the binary's arguments only after `--`, where `cargo run` passes the first
-plain argument and everything after it. Make `run` take them the same way, `--` needed only when
-the binary's first argument is a flag or one of `run`'s own.
-* `args` is clap's `trailing_var_arg` with `allow_hyphen_values`, in place of `last`: the first
-  argument that is not `run`'s own starts the binary's, and everything after it is the binary's,
-  flags and a later `--bin` included, as cargo does.
-  - `--` is needed only before one of `run`'s own, `--bin`, `-h`, or `--help`: `cx run -- --help`
-    hands `--help` to the binary, `cx run --help` shows `run`'s.
-  - The cost: an unknown flag first, a mistyped `--bni` say, reaches the binary rather than being
-    refused, an acceptable trade for a run wrapper.
-* The parse test pins each case, and cargo's own `Running` line shows the binary given `foo -x --bin
-  b` and `--help`.
-* Completion follows the same split.
-  - `cx run --bin <tab>` offers the workspace's binaries, read by `cargo metadata` on each tab,
-    xtask's own left out, by `xtask-lib`'s `metadata`, now public.
-  - Once the binary's arguments have begun, `cx run foo <tab>` and `cx run -- <tab>` offer nothing,
-    where they offered `--bin` and `--help`, which would have reached the binary.
-  - clap's engine ignores `trailing_var_arg` when completing, offering a command's options beside
-    any positional whose minimum is met, always for a `Vec`, and has no knob for it. So `main`
-    answers such a request with nothing before clap is asked, `xtask-lib`'s
-    `binary_args_started` deciding it from the request's words and index.
-  - Completing the binary's own arguments waits for it to have a CLI, `io-uring-x1` having none.

-  subsection stays as it was, this rung superseding it.

-The ring's depths are fixed, 8 SQEs and the kernel's default of twice as many CQEs. Make both
-optional: an SQ depth, and a CQ depth by `IORING_SETUP_CQSIZE`, on `Ring` and as the binary's

-  and `Ring::with_depths` sets them up, `Ring::new(entries)` staying as the SQ-only shorthand.
-  - A named CQ is asked for by `IORING_SETUP_CQSIZE` with `cq_entries`, the kernel rounding it up
-    to a power of two as it does the SQ's.
-  - Tests pin the kernel's answers: a CQ of 32 over an SQ of 4, 5 rounded to 8, a CQ equal to
-    the SQ, and the refusals, a CQ smaller than the SQ and a zero depth either way, each
-    `EINVAL`.

-  parsing.
-  - Its `-V` is clap's `version`, since `vc-x1 install` runs `-V` to read the version it installs,
-    and a CLI without it refused the flag and failed the install.
-  - The round trip sends its four NOPs in batches the SQ holds, submitting and reaping each, so an
-    SQ smaller than four works, `--sq-entries 2` taking two batches.
-  - The kernel's refusal is a bare `EINVAL`, so `main` names the depths it refused and the rule
-    beside it.

-  after the binary's first flag, the binary still having no completion of its own.

-* `run` has clap's `disable_help_flag`, so `-h` and `--help` are ordinary arguments and, with
-  `allow_hyphen_values`, the binary's: `cx run -h` and `cx run --bin io-uring-x1 -h` print the app's
-  help, as `cx run -- -h` did.
-  - `run`'s own help is clap's `help` task, `cx help run`, and its long help says so.
-  - `--bin` is `run`'s one flag, and `--` is needed only before a `--bin` meant for the binary.
-  - A difference from cargo, accepted: `cargo run -h` is cargo's help, and `cx run -h` the app's,

-  `--bin` alone and `cx run -h <tab>` nothing.

-Two spsc queues in front of the ring: a request queue whose entries become SQEs, and a completion
-queue the CQEs are copied into, so a caller never touches the ring itself.

-  queue's producer, and `step(wait)` moves what it can: requests into SQEs, the SQ into the kernel,
-  CQEs into completions. `NopRequest { user_data }` and `NopCompletion { user_data, res, flags }`
-  are the slots' `#[repr(C)]` zerocopy messages.
-  - Backpressure, nothing dropped: a request is released only once its SQE is published, a read
-    slot dropped otherwise re-delivering it, and a completion slot is reserved before its CQE is
-    popped, a write slot dropped otherwise abandoning it, so a full completion queue leaves CQEs
-    in the CQ.

-    the CQ has room for, no CQ overflow possible.
-  - `step(true)` with something in flight waits in the kernel for one completion, so an idle
-    driver sleeps rather than spins.

-  sizing it, one segment per queue, in-process.

-    `Debug` text and `main` names each queue's.
-  - It is a path dependency on the sibling checkout `../zc-ring-x1`, so a build takes whatever that
-    working copy holds, here its `main` at `e705b50d`, version `0.19.5`, and a clone without the
-    sibling does not build. Pinning it, a git dependency at a commit, is for when zc-ring-x1's API settles.

-  queue of 2 holds CQEs back, 4 in flight and 2 completed, until the caller drains all 8. The
-  second assumes a NOP completes during its submit, which 200 runs bore out.
-* `main` runs the caller and the driver on two threads, the io_uring made on the driver's, its
-  pointers never crossing, the spsc endpoints `Send`. The caller's waits end if the driver stops,
-  so a refused setup reports and exits rather than hanging, and the output's order is fixed,
-  setup, completions, final state. It runs at one-entry rings, 100 runs.

-Closing out the cycle.

-  among its tests, and `io-uring-x1` printing four NOPs out of the completion queue, each with its
-  `user_data` and `res` 0.

-  long, and zero-copy across processes, is [io-uring.md](notes/io-uring.md), much of it from the
-  cycle's discussion rather than its rungs, and `README.md` names the ring, the driver, and the

-  trait and vc-x1's ladder marker, it became a Todo here and a message to send, never an edit

content.content:
## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version. The bump is the project's, by its own tool, and `vc-x1` never
writes a version: with `[version] file` and `pattern` in the config it refuses a commit that
leaves the version's line unchanged, and `--same-version` commits it as it is.

## Agent-files version

Depend on zc-ring-x1 by `git = "https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` and `tag =
"v0.19.7"` in `Cargo.toml`, the `path` dropped, and let `Cargo.lock` record the git source at
`8cc34343`, so every build takes the tagged commit whatever `../zc-ring-x1` holds.

`Cargo.lock` gives zc-ring-x1 0.19.7 the source
`git+https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git?tag=v0.19.7#8cc34343...`, `cargo xtask validate`
passes, and a clone of the cycle's tip into a directory with no `zc-ring-x1` sibling builds with
`cargo build --locked` and passes `cargo test`.

- The tag, not a `rev`: zc-ring-x1 tags every Land now, so a tag names the version as the manifest
  does and a later move is a one-word edit. `Cargo.lock` holds the commit, so a moved tag cannot
  change a `--locked` build silently.
- v0.19.7, not v0.19.5: the working copy's `Cargo.lock` already builds against 0.19.7, taken from
  the sibling path, so the pin keeps the code that builds today.
- `version = "0.19.7"` is kept beside the git source, so Cargo checks the tagged commit's manifest
  against it.

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).

### feat: build and install by cargo xtask

`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` in `.vc-config.md` are the project's knowledge in vc-x1's
config, as `[validate]` was before `cargo xtask validate`. Move them into xtask, `cargo xtask install
--profile dev` for one, with a `custom.md` override where the agent-files name `vc-x1 install`.

### feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags

`io-uring-x1` has a CLI, `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`, and no completion. Give it clap's
`CompleteEnv`, as xtask has, so `source <(COMPLETE=bash io-uring-x1)` registers it, and
`io-uring-x1-dev` its own the same way. The depths complete to the powers of two up to the kernel's
limits, 32768 for the SQ and 65536 for the CQ, the values the kernel rounds to. It needs
`clap_complete` with `unstable-dynamic`, as xtask's does.

### feat: cx run hands completion to the binary

Once the binary's arguments have begun, `cargo xtask run` completes nothing, where it could ask the
binary. In `xtask-lib`'s `run`, run the built `target/debug/<bin>` with `COMPLETE=bash`, the words
after `run` given with the binary's name first, and relay its answer, so `cx run --sq-entries <tab>`
offers the depths. A tab never builds: no binary built, no completion, and one a build behind
completes a build behind. Waits on `feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags`, and serves any
binary with `CompleteEnv`.

### refactor: read cargo metadata into typed structs

`xtask-lib`'s `run` reads `cargo metadata` as a `serde_json::Value`, indexed by name, so a typo or a
schema change reads as a silent `Null`, and `binaries` falls back with `unwrap_or(&empty)` twice.
Deserialize into `Metadata`, `Package`, and `Target` structs with serde's derive, owned `String`s,
so a missing field is a parse error and the fallbacks go. Clarity, not speed: the parse is
microseconds beside the `cargo metadata` process.

### feat: share the xtask library across repos

This cycle makes xtask a library within this workspace. Moving it into its own repo, a git or path
dependency, lets vc-x1, whose xtask this one was modelled on, and other projects use one copy.

## Ideas

Items not yet solid enough for `## Todo`. Triaged at the next opening: promote, fold into a
picked-up cycle, or drop.

## Bugs

_See [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md).

## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path

#### Problem

`zc-ring-x1` is a path dependency on `../zc-ring-x1`, so a build takes whatever that working copy
holds and a clone without the sibling does not build. Switch to `git =
"https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` at `tag = "v0.19.7"` (`8cc34343`), the latest tag,
zc-ring-x1 having tagged its versions in reply to `m-12` in `../vc-x1-messages`. `core::error::Error`
for zc-ring-x1's error types, so `?` reaches `Box<dyn Error>`, was not asked, and is a later message
if it is wanted.

#### Solution

Depend on zc-ring-x1 by `git = "https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` and `tag =
"v0.19.7"` in `Cargo.toml`, the `path` dropped, and let `Cargo.lock` record the git source at
`8cc34343`, so every build takes the tagged commit whatever `../zc-ring-x1` holds.

#### Acceptance check

`Cargo.lock` gives zc-ring-x1 0.19.7 the source
`git+https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git?tag=v0.19.7#8cc34343...`, `cargo xtask validate`
passes, and a clone of the cycle's tip into a directory with no `zc-ring-x1` sibling builds with
`cargo build --locked` and passes `cargo test`.

#### Deliberation

- The tag, not a `rev`: zc-ring-x1 tags every Land now, so a tag names the version as the manifest
  does and a later move is a one-word edit. `Cargo.lock` holds the commit, so a moved tag cannot
  change a `--locked` build silently.
- v0.19.7, not v0.19.5: the working copy's `Cargo.lock` already builds against 0.19.7, taken from
  the sibling path, so the pin keeps the code that builds today.
- `version = "0.19.7"` is kept beside the git source, so Cargo checks the tagged commit's manifest
  against it.

### feat: build and install by cargo xtask

`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` in `.vc-config.md` are the project's knowledge in vc-x1's
config, as `[validate]` was before `cargo xtask validate`. Move them into xtask, `cargo xtask install
--profile dev` for one, with a `custom.md` override where the agent-files name `vc-x1 install`.

### feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags

`io-uring-x1` has a CLI, `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`, and no completion. Give it clap's
`CompleteEnv`, as xtask has, so `source <(COMPLETE=bash io-uring-x1)` registers it, and
`io-uring-x1-dev` its own the same way. The depths complete to the powers of two up to the kernel's
limits, 32768 for the SQ and 65536 for the CQ, the values the kernel rounds to. It needs
`clap_complete` with `unstable-dynamic`, as xtask's does.

### feat: cx run hands completion to the binary

Once the binary's arguments have begun, `cargo xtask run` completes nothing, where it could ask the
binary. In `xtask-lib`'s `run`, run the built `target/debug/<bin>` with `COMPLETE=bash`, the words
after `run` given with the binary's name first, and relay its answer, so `cx run --sq-entries <tab>`
offers the depths. A tab never builds: no binary built, no completion, and one a build behind
completes a build behind. Waits on `feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags`, and serves any
binary with `CompleteEnv`.

### refactor: read cargo metadata into typed structs

`xtask-lib`'s `run` reads `cargo metadata` as a `serde_json::Value`, indexed by name, so a typo or a
schema change reads as a silent `Null`, and `binaries` falls back with `unwrap_or(&empty)` twice.
Deserialize into `Metadata`, `Package`, and `Target` structs with serde's derive, owned `String`s,
so a missing field is a parse error and the fallbacks go. Clarity, not speed: the parse is
microseconds beside the `cargo metadata` process.

This cycle makes xtask a library within this workspace. Moving it into its own repo, a git or path
dependency, lets vc-x1, whose xtask this one was modelled on, and other projects use one copy.

the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path

#### Problem

`zc-ring-x1` is a path dependency on `../zc-ring-x1`, so a build takes whatever that working copy
holds and a clone without the sibling does not build. Switch to `git =
"https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` at `tag = "v0.19.7"` (`8cc34343`), the latest tag,
zc-ring-x1 having tagged its versions in reply to `m-12` in `../vc-x1-messages`. `core::error::Error`
for zc-ring-x1's error types, so `?` reaches `Box<dyn Error>`, was not asked, and is a later message
if it is wanted.

#### Solution

Depend on zc-ring-x1 by `git = "https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` and `tag =
"v0.19.7"` in `Cargo.toml`, the `path` dropped, and let `Cargo.lock` record the git source at
`8cc34343`, so every build takes the tagged commit whatever `../zc-ring-x1` holds.

#### Acceptance check

`Cargo.lock` gives zc-ring-x1 0.19.7 the source
`git+https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git?tag=v0.19.7#8cc34343...`, `cargo xtask validate`
passes, and a clone of the cycle's tip into a directory with no `zc-ring-x1` sibling builds with
`cargo build --locked` and passes `cargo test`.

#### Deliberation

- The tag, not a `rev`: zc-ring-x1 tags every Land now, so a tag names the version as the manifest
  does and a later move is a one-word edit. `Cargo.lock` holds the commit, so a moved tag cannot
  change a `--locked` build silently.
- v0.19.7, not v0.19.5: the working copy's `Cargo.lock` already builds against 0.19.7, taken from
  the sibling path, so the pin keeps the code that builds today.
- `version = "0.19.7"` is kept beside the git source, so Cargo checks the tagged commit's manifest
  against it.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).

### feat: build and install by cargo xtask

`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` in `.vc-config.md` are the project's knowledge in vc-x1's
config, as `[validate]` was before `cargo xtask validate`. Move them into xtask, `cargo xtask install
--profile dev` for one, with a `custom.md` override where the agent-files name `vc-x1 install`.

### feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags

`io-uring-x1` has a CLI, `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`, and no completion. Give it clap's
`CompleteEnv`, as xtask has, so `source <(COMPLETE=bash io-uring-x1)` registers it, and
`io-uring-x1-dev` its own the same way. The depths complete to the powers of two up to the kernel's
limits, 32768 for the SQ and 65536 for the CQ, the values the kernel rounds to. It needs
`clap_complete` with `unstable-dynamic`, as xtask's does.

### feat: cx run hands completion to the binary

Once the binary's arguments have begun, `cargo xtask run` completes nothing, where it could ask the
binary. In `xtask-lib`'s `run`, run the built `target/debug/<bin>` with `COMPLETE=bash`, the words
after `run` given with the binary's name first, and relay its answer, so `cx run --sq-entries <tab>`
offers the depths. A tab never builds: no binary built, no completion, and one a build behind
completes a build behind. Waits on `feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags`, and serves any
binary with `CompleteEnv`.

### refactor: read cargo metadata into typed structs

`xtask-lib`'s `run` reads `cargo metadata` as a `serde_json::Value`, indexed by name, so a typo or a
schema change reads as a silent `Null`, and `binaries` falls back with `unwrap_or(&empty)` twice.
Deserialize into `Metadata`, `Package`, and `Target` structs with serde's derive, owned `String`s,
so a missing field is a parse error and the fallbacks go. Clarity, not speed: the parse is
microseconds beside the `cargo metadata` process.

### feat: share the xtask library across repos

This cycle makes xtask a library within this workspace. Moving it into its own repo, a git or path
dependency, lets vc-x1, whose xtask this one was modelled on, and other projects use one copy.

picked-up cycle, or drop.

_See [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md).

restating one, so a change is a single edit and the copies cannot drift. Consolidated 2026-08-09,

- **Prose**, all durable text: wrap at <=100 cols, bullet continuations indented two spaces.
- **Source**, doc comments and inline comments included: <=100 cols, which is rustfmt's default
  `max_width` (enforcement notes in [code.md](code.md#line-width)).
- **Commit titles**: <=50 chars.
- **Commit bodies**: <=75 cols, the Linux kernel patch standard. It replaced git's older 72
  convention here 2026-08-09, and published bodies keep the wrap they shipped with.

The widths are wrap defaults, not absolutes (the title cap excepted). Existing text re-wraps when
touched, no mass sweeps. Write to the full width: wrap near the limit rather than imitating the
narrow wrap of older text, and a line that reads better long stays long (an URL, a literal report
row, indented code in a comment).

### Problem-first shape

`## In Progress` cycle blocks, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a sharper form of the same
shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.

- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences. Don't pad with intent, don't restate what
  follows it.
- **Solution statement** (the what/how): what is done about the problem, in broad terms, answering
  whatever question the problem statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in [Bullet content
  differs by surface](#prose-form) above.
- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), the steps. Formality differs by surface:
  - In Progress: a committed ladder, one step per commit. See [Conventional-commit
    shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) for the per-step title + `(current)` /
    `(done)` form.
  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering, formalized only when the entry is picked up
    into a cycle.

**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A cycle
writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land. The close-out's commit
body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a commit body's
is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule here said a plan
was for work not yet done and a solution for work that is, which left a cycle unable to say at its
opening what it intended to do.

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is two plain paragraphs, and the
rung's subsection in the record holds the full account, so the breakdown is written once.

- **The solution**, opening "Solution:", ending with the pointer to the record where it is at that

# Todo and cycle record

This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record, read first at
acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.

_None._

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path

#### Problem

`zc-ring-x1` is a path dependency on `../zc-ring-x1`, so a build takes whatever that working copy
holds and a clone without the sibling does not build. Switch to `git =
"https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` at `tag = "v0.19.7"` (`8cc34343`), the latest tag,
zc-ring-x1 having tagged its versions in reply to `m-12` in `../vc-x1-messages`. `core::error::Error`
for zc-ring-x1's error types, so `?` reaches `Box<dyn Error>`, was not asked, and is a later message
if it is wanted.

#### Solution

`Cargo.toml` names zc-ring-x1 by `git = "https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git"` and `tag =
"v0.19.7"`, the `path` dropped, and `Cargo.lock` records the git source at `8cc34343`, so every
build takes the tagged commit whatever `../zc-ring-x1` holds.

#### Acceptance check

`Cargo.lock` gives zc-ring-x1 0.19.7 the source
`git+https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1.git?tag=v0.19.7#8cc34343...`, `cargo xtask validate`
passes, and a clone of the cycle's tip into a directory with no `zc-ring-x1` sibling builds with
`cargo build --locked` and passes `cargo test`.

#### Deliberation

- The tag, not a `rev`: zc-ring-x1 tags every Land now, so a tag names the version as the manifest
  does and a later move is a one-word edit. `Cargo.lock` holds the commit, so a moved tag cannot
  change a `--locked` build silently.
- v0.19.7, not v0.19.5: the working copy's `Cargo.lock` already builds against 0.19.7, taken from
  the sibling path, so the pin keeps the code that builds today.
- `version = "0.19.7"` is kept beside the git source, so Cargo checks the tagged commit's manifest
  against it.
- Single-step, not a ladder: the change is one manifest line and the lockfile it implies, so the
  planned work rung was dropped and the cycle is one commit.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path opening

The cycle's first commit, carrying its plan: the bookmark, the last cycle's record deleted, and the
Todo entry moved into this block.

##### build: pin zc-ring-x1 by git, not the sibling path closing

Closing out the cycle.

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition and
promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

_None._

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).

### feat: build and install by cargo xtask

`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` in `.vc-config.md` are the project's knowledge in vc-x1's
config, as `[validate]` was before `cargo xtask validate`. Move them into xtask, `cargo xtask install
--profile dev` for one, with a `custom.md` override where the agent-files name `vc-x1 install`.

### feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags

`io-uring-x1` has a CLI, `--sq-entries` and `--cq-entries`, and no completion. Give it clap's
`CompleteEnv`, as xtask has, so `source <(COMPLETE=bash io-uring-x1)` registers it, and
`io-uring-x1-dev` its own the same way. The depths complete to the powers of two up to the kernel's
limits, 32768 for the SQ and 65536 for the CQ, the values the kernel rounds to. It needs
`clap_complete` with `unstable-dynamic`, as xtask's does.

### feat: cx run hands completion to the binary

Once the binary's arguments have begun, `cargo xtask run` completes nothing, where it could ask the
binary. In `xtask-lib`'s `run`, run the built `target/debug/<bin>` with `COMPLETE=bash`, the words
after `run` given with the binary's name first, and relay its answer, so `cx run --sq-entries <tab>`
offers the depths. A tab never builds: no binary built, no completion, and one a build behind
completes a build behind. Waits on `feat: io-uring-x1 completes its own flags`, and serves any
binary with `CompleteEnv`.

### refactor: read cargo metadata into typed structs

`xtask-lib`'s `run` reads `cargo metadata` as a `serde_json::Value`, indexed by name, so a typo or a
schema change reads as a silent `Null`, and `binaries` falls back with `unwrap_or(&empty)` twice.
Deserialize into `Metadata`, `Package`, and `Target` structs with serde's derive, owned `String`s,
so a missing field is a parse error and the fallbacks go. Clarity, not speed: the parse is
microseconds beside the `cargo metadata` process.

### feat: share the xtask library across repos

This cycle makes xtask a library within this workspace. Moving it into its own repo, a git or path
dependency, lets vc-x1, whose xtask this one was modelled on, and other projects use one copy.
